chapter: The war years: Barnet, Hot Lips Page, Newton and Kirby
title: USO unit, Kenneth Spencer and Cafe Society acts
summary: He was in the first all-Black USO unit, was meant for Russia with Kenneth Spencer, played Cafe Society acts, and recalls singer Aubrey Pankey.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years

blocks.x: Now, I don't want to go into this, it isn't my area, but I was also in Cuba during the War. I represented the first all so-called Black unit of the USO, the first experimental... Primarily I was in... I was also in Cafe

Society, which is when I came to (?). Primarily I was to go to Russia to... Russia was our ally at that time, and Kenneth Spencer was selected to sing for the Russian troops, and I was to go with him. Somehow or other it came about... Somehow I was diverted into an all-Black unit to go somewhere else.
What sort of singer was he?

He was a Classical singer, sang spirituals -- like Paul Robeson. He was in the picture in Bataan. "Mon Amore..." Which leads me right... I played with (?) for him in Cafe Society along with Josh White, along with Betty Comden, and I played that act with Betty Comden and Adolph Green, and Judy Holiday, when they used to do a night... They used to feature a song called "A Night In Philadelphia".

There was also a singer named Aubrey Pankey.
Ironically, to divert back to the days when I took this train, when I was stranded in Europe and took this train... There was an ex-drummer on that train, and I stood up all the way, ninety miles, and we talked -- and this drummer's name was Aubrey Pankey. When he got back to the States, he dropped the drums and became a concert singer.
